subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw implement heading-aware chunking now as a scoped memory-core strategy, make it the default chunker behavior, or defer it until the broader entity/graph memory design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product choice affects current users' index identity, config surface, retrieval defaults, and the boundary between memory-core and Memory Wiki/entity extraction.

options.title: Scoped opt-in strategy
options.body: Add a heading/section-aware memory-core chunking strategy with explicit index identity, docs, and tests while leaving entity extraction as separate Memory MVP or Memory Wiki design work.

options.title: Default heading-aware chunking
options.body: Change the default chunker to respect headings, accepting broader upgrade-proof requirements for existing headed memory files.

options.title: Defer for unified memory design
options.body: Hold the chunking change until maintainers settle the entity, graph, and compiled-memory architecture so the retrieval and knowledge layers land together.

recommendation.title: Scoped opt-in strategy
recommendation.body: Add a heading/section-aware memory-core chunking strategy with explicit index identity, docs, and tests while leaving entity extraction as separate Memory MVP or Memory Wiki design work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history across the current chunker, memory-core indexing, and index metadata files that would define the contract.
